{{nihongo|'''Kamo Shrine'''|鴨神社 (高槻市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Kamo Shrine''' (かもじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Takatsuki|Q335423|qid=Q335423}}, Osaka Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current enshrined deities are as follows<ref>The enshrined deities are based on [http://kamojinja.web.fc2.com/kamojinja01.html History of Kamo Shrine] (official website). Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto is treated as a deity of special status among them, according to the same site and the shrine register displayed within the precincts.</ref>.
* '''{{ill|Ōyamatsumi|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto}}'''
* {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Izanami|ar|إزانامي|az|İzanami|bcl|Izanami|bs|Izanami|ca|Izanami|da|Izanami|el|Ιζανάμι|eo|Izanami|es|Izanami|fa|ایزانامی|fi|Izanami|fr|Izanami|he|איזאנמי|hr|Izanami|hu|Izanami|hy|Իզանամի|id|Izanami|it|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|ko|이자나미|mk|Изанами|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯃꯤ|pt|Izanami|rsk|Изанами|ru|Идзанами|simple|Izanami|sl|Izanami|sr|Изанами|sv|Izanami|ta|இசநமி|th|อิซานามิ|tl|Izanami|tr|Izanami|uk|Ідзанамі|zh|伊邪那美|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Kamotaketsunumi no Mikoto|Q11634939|qid=Q11634939|lt=Kamo no Mioya Ōkami}}

Various documents such as the “Shrine Register” list the enshrined deity as Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami, but as described below, according to the theory that identifies this shrine as the Shikinaisha Mishima Kamo Shrine, the enshrined deity is considered to be the ancestral deity of the Kamo clan<ref name="place"/>. In addition, since this area was a place where the Mishima Agatanushi held power, there is also a theory that regards their ancestral deity as the enshrined deity<ref name="place"/>. The “{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}” records that the Mishima no Sukune (descendants of the Mishima Agatanushi, Jingibetsu of the Right Capital) and the Kamo Agatanushi (Jingibetsu of Yamashiro Province) share the same ancestor<ref name="place"/>.

=== History ===
=== Foundation ===
The date of foundation is unknown. According to shrine tradition, it was originally established by the resident Kamo clan, and later came to be known as “Mishima Kamo Shrine” because the immigrant Mishima clan rose to power in the area<ref>[http://kamojinja.web.fc2.com/kamojinja03.html The original tutelary deity of Settsu–Mishima] (official website).</ref>.

=== Historical overview ===
In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the “{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}” lists “Mishima Kamo Shrine, Shimashimo District, Settsu Province” as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}. Since Yukihiko Ambo pointed out in “Historical Sites and Scenic Places of Mishima District” that the “Osaka Prefecture Shrine Register” states: “Although there are no old records, it has long been handed down that the enshrined deity is Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto; the place of enshrinement was formerly called Shimashimo District (this village was originally in Shimashimo District and was incorporated into Shimakami District during the Tokugawa era) … it has also been popularly called Mishima Kamo, Go-i Kamo Shrine, or Mishima Shrine,” this shrine has been regarded as one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for the Engishiki Mishima Kamo Shrine.

Another candidate shrine for the Shikinaisha is {{ill|Mishima-Kamo Shrine|Q11355295|qid=Q11355295}} located in Mishimae. Since Mishima Kamo Shrine lies within {{ill|Shimakami district|Q10965808|qid=Q10965808}}, this shrine is considered more plausible in terms of district boundaries<ref name="place">“Place Names of Osaka Prefecture,” entry on Kamo Shrine.</ref>. On the other hand, an excerpt from the “Iyo Province Fudoki” records that Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami moved from “Mishima of Tsukushi Province” to Iyo, and since the deity is also called the “God of the Crossing,” it has been argued that Kamo Shrine, which is distant from rivers, does not fit this description<ref>Matsushita Akira, “Mishima Kamo Shrine,” in Ken’ichi Tanigawa (ed.), “Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Sites – Vol. 3: Settsu, Kawachi, Izumi, Awaji” ({{ill|Hakusuisha Publishing|Q4346470|qid=Q4346470}}).</ref>. In any case, no definitive conclusion has been reached.

At the end of the Heian period, it is said that {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|Q317984|qid=Q317984}}’s consort {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kenreimon-in}} prayed at “Mishima Shrine” for the birth of a prince<ref name="ka1">[http://kamojinja.web.fc2.com/kamojinja01.html History of Kamo Shrine] (official website).</ref>. As a result, the future {{ill|Emperor Takakura|Q357261|qid=Q357261}} was born, and to celebrate this, Mishima Shrine was founded at Gojozaka in Kyoto<ref name="ka2"/>. However, the place of her worship is recorded as “Mishima Shrine,” and there is also a theory that this refers to Mishima Kamo Shrine at Mishimae<ref name="ka2">[http://kamojinja.web.fc2.com/120504-02.html Kamo Shrine Newsletter] (official website).</ref>.

In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 46 ({{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}}), the main hall and worship hall were newly constructed.

=== Court rank ===
* {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 8 ({{ill|884|Q23895|qid=Q23895}}), December 21: promoted from Senior Sixth Rank, Upper Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade (“{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}”) – recorded as “Mishima Shrine.” There is also a theory that this refers to {{ill|Mishima-Kamo Shrine|Q11355295|qid=Q11355295}}.
